## 🌍 Overview

This PR implements the complete **Environment Management** feature for DRUT.  
Users can now create named environments containing key-value pairs and inject them dynamically into URLs and request bodies using `{{VAR}}` syntax.

---

## ✅ What's Included

### 🧠 Context Logic

- `EnvContext.tsx`: Global context to manage multiple named environments
  - `addEnv`, `updateEnv`, `deleteEnv`, `selectEnv`
  - Tracks `selectedEnvId`
  - Stores to and loads from **IndexedDB via localforage**

### 🔄 Resolver

- `envResolver.ts`: Replaces `{{VAR}}` syntax with values from selected env
- Used inside `RequestBuilder.tsx` before sending request

### 💾 Persistence

- All environments stored in IndexedDB (`localforage`)
- Selected environment is persisted between reloads

---

## 💻 UI Components

- `EnvPage.tsx`: Main page to manage environments
- `EnvList.tsx`: Lists all environments
- `EnvEditor.tsx`: Form to add/edit environments
- `EnvSelector.tsx`: Dropdown injected in request form for selecting active env

All components are built using **React Bootstrap** for consistent styling.

---

## 🧪 Testing

- ✅ `EnvContext.test.ts`: Full coverage of add/update/delete/select/load
- ✅ `EnvList.test.tsx`: Render, edit, delete
- ✅ `EnvEditor.test.tsx`: Full form logic, add/remove vars, submit, cancel
- ✅ `EnvSelector.test.tsx`: Select event fires
- ✅ `EnvPage.test.tsx`: Integration render
- ✅ `envResolver.test.ts`: Resolves multiple/missing variables

🎯 **100% code coverage** on all components and context logic.

---

## 💅 Code Style & Structure

- Follows Prettier config:
  - `"singleQuote": true`, `"semi": false`, `"trailingComma": "es5"`
- Strong typing on all components/hooks
- Folder structure respected (`components/Env`, `context/`, `lib/`)

---

## 🧭 Routing & Integration

- Page mounted at `/env`
- Added `EnvSelector` to `RequestBuilder` for runtime substitution

---

author: davidz25
body:
Change onFrameCaptured() so it doesn't return an ImageBitmap which was intended to be used for the application to overlay graphics. Instead, if users want to overlay graphics they can simply arrange their composition so a `Canvas` overlays the `Camera` composable.

Use platform-native types for the returned frame - on Android this is an ImageProxy and on iOS it's an UIImage. Note that the captured frame is different sizes/rotation/etc from the preview. To deal with this, pass a Matrix in CameraFrame so the application can properly transform into preview space.

Hook this up to barcode scanning and also in CameraScreen have use-cases that use the preview (drawing an animation on top) and don't use the previes (just showing an Image with the captured bitmap).

Test: Manually tested barcode scanning on both Android and iOS.

* Rename "incidence matrix" to "adjacency matrix".

> Usage: ride-faker.js [--help] --beacon-hash beacon_hash --routekey routeKeyStr [--tick-interval miliseconds] routeFile
> 
> A development utility to post coordinates to a route's beacon page, which
> will simulate a bike bus moving along the route.
> 
>  Options:
>     --beacon-hash|-b    Required. The `beacon_hash` value to use when
>                         POSTing. If not supplied, will use the Environment
>                         variable `beacon_hash`, if it exists and is set
>     --help|-h           show this text and exit
>     --routekey|-k       Required. The routeKey to be used when POSTing
>                         locations to the API
>     --tick-interval|-t  Time, in miliseconds, to wait between POSTing the
>                         next coordinates along the route. Default: 15000
> 
>  routeFile:
>     path to a route file, though the file need not neccessarily be a route
>     route file. The only thing that the JSON file needs to have is an array
>     with a key named `stop` underneath a key that matches the values supplied
>     to --routekey

It's pretty straight forward, I think. Also it's just a dev tool, so it doesn't have to be great.

The one part about it that is a little funky is that if "stops" are > 100m apart the script will create several in between coordinates to move to, so that the coordinates don't jump a huge amount at one time. Which I feel clever about.
